verified_nodes.evidence: This node is a capital-source stage, not a manufactured-goods stage, so its true "supplier" in the strict sense is a monopoly: the US federal government is the only entity that can originate Title 23 TA Set-Aside dollars, Title 49 FTA formula/CIG dollars, or a discretionary program like ATIIP or Bus/Low-No; no company substitutes for that appropriation, which is why substitutability is scored 4 (not 5, because states, municipal bonds, and value-capture financing are partial, if much smaller and slower, alternatives; not lower, because at TA's USD 1.44 billion/year and CIG's multi-billion pipeline scale, non-federal sources cannot fully backfill in the near term). Capacity is constrained less by physical throughput than by appropriation ceiling and competition for it: TA formula funds are fixed by statute (59 percent suballocated by population per highways.dot.gov's TA fact sheet), but FY2024 TA obligations of USD 973.3 million against a larger pool of eligible requests, and ATIIP's single completed round being oversubscribed 40 to 1 (railstotrails.org factsheet), show the discretionary layer is demand-constrained well beyond available dollars, which is the binding constraint the pathway inherits downstream. On cost share: federal-aid highway funds including the TA Set-Aside can cover up to 80 percent of an eligible project's cost under 23 U.S.C. 133, with a minimum non-federal match near 20 percent, while FTA Capital Investment Grants cap the federal share at 60 percent for New Starts and up to 80 percent for Small Starts under 49 U.S.C. 5309; blending these statutory caps against typical local match practice gives a rough delivered-unit federal cost share near 0.5, i.e. federal formula and discretionary money funds roughly half the all-in cost of a typical bike/transit infrastructure unit once state and local match, land, and soft costs are included. Downstream, the private companies that actually convert this appropriation into revenue are engineering/program-management firms holding on-call contracts with state DOTs and transit agencies (AECOM, Jacobs, WSP, Tetra Tech, ICF, plus large private firms HNTB, HDR, STV, Kimley-Horn) and Buy-America-compliant vehicle manufacturers selling into FTA-funded bus and rail procurements (NFI Group/New Flyer, REV Group/ElDorado, Gillig private, Alstom, Siemens Mobility); that segment is comparatively commoditized, with many qualified bidders competing for federal-aid task orders, so it should not be confused with the financing node itself, which is genuinely concentrated in one funder. Three lines of counter-evidence undercut the "sole source / high-control" framing:

1. Substitutes exist and already operate at comparable or larger scale than this node. The claim's own cost_share of 0.5 means non-federal capital already funds roughly half of a typical project by the claim's own math, which is inconsistent with treating the federal appropriation as the pathway's rate-limiting input. Beyond that baseline match, large parallel non-federal capital channels fund the same urban-mobility shift independent of Title 23/49 appropriations: local-option sales-tax transit measures (Sound Transit ST3, a roughly $54 billion 25-year package funded by local sales/MVET/property tax, and LA Metro's Measure M, a permanent local sales tax projected near $860 million/year) dwarf the ~$1.44 billion/year federal TA Set-Aside in scale; state-funded programs such as California's Active Transportation Program run on state gas-tax/cap-and-trade revenue at a scale comparable to the federal set-aside; and the e-bike/micromobility side of the shift is funded mostly through state and city rebate programs (e.g., California's statewide e-bike incentive project, Denver's e-bike rebate) and private consumer/VC capital, which bypass this node entirely. Municipal GO bonds, TIFIA/private-activity-bond financing, and P3 capital are further substitutes the claim itself acknowledges as "partial" but does not weight heavily enough given their demonstrated scale.

2. Capacity is not tightly bound at the layer that actually carries most of the flow. The claim's evidence for capacity constraint (ATIIP oversubscribed 40:1) is drawn from a small, one-time discretionary competition, not from the much larger formula-based TA Set-Aside or FTA formula programs (5307/5339), which carry statutory flex-transfer authority between highway and transit categories (23 U.S.C. 133 / 49 U.S.C. 5307) and have historically carried forward large unobligated Highway Trust Fund balances. That is spare capacity, not a binding ceiling, at the layer this node's cost_share actually depends on.

3. The pathway has repeatedly proceeded through funding-authorization gaps rather than stopping at them: the claim's own text notes Congress has historically bridged authorization lapses (FAST Act to IIJA, and the current IIJA-to-BUILD-America-250 transition) with continuing resolutions rather than a hard funding cliff, and state DOTs commonly advance projects on state funds during such gaps. A step whose interruption is routinely absorbed downstream without halting the correction is not acting as the rate-limiting step in the metabolic-control-analysis sense the framework invokes.

Net: this node is a real and meaningful capital input, but it is one of several substitutable, largely non-capacity-bound financing channels feeding the urban-mobility correction, not a monopoly bottleneck. Corrected substitutability 2 (real, sizable non-federal alternatives already operating at comparable or larger scale) and capacity_constraint 2 (formula-layer flexibility and historical unobligated carryover; only a small discretionary sub-program shows tight capacity) both push flux control well below the claimed 0.84.

Only heavy/light rail (3-6+ years) is a real constraint, but rail car procurement is confined to a handful of legacy US metros (NYC, Boston, Chicago, DC, Philly, LA, SF) and is largely decoupled from the worldwide, bike/e-bike/micromobility-centered mode-shift correction the framework is scoring -- most growing cities in the correction's scope (Asia, Africa, Latin America, mid-size US/EU cities) are not buying heavy rail cars at all. (4) The rail bench itself is deeper than "high control" implies: Siemens, Alstom, Kawasaki, Stadler, CAF, Hyundai Rotem all field credible US-capable trainsets -- oligopoly, not sole-source. (5) Foreign-entity-of-concern restrictions are a multi-year-telegraphed reallocation among many remaining Western/allied suppliers (announced in the 2021 infrastructure law, phasing to 2029), not an acute unplanned bottleneck -- exactly the kind of years-ahead-signaled shift the framework treats as normal niche construction, not a control chokepoint. Net: this looks like a moderate, competitively-supplied, easily-forecast layer whose true economic weight in the corrected pathway is smaller than claimed, not a rate-limiting step.

verified_nodes.evidence: Concentration: the four branded drive-unit makers (Bosch ~25 percent, Shimano ~20 percent, Bafang ~15 percent, Yamaha ~10 percent) hold about 70 percent of the global e-bike drive-unit market between them, per GM Insights and Best Bike Brands comparative data. Consolidation in real time: Yamaha absorbed Brose's e-bike drive-unit business on Aug 1, 2025, removing one of the few remaining independent mid-drive suppliers and further concentrating the node (electrive.com). Cost share: no manufacturer discloses a drive-unit-only bill-of-materials line item, but two independent proxies converge on roughly 8-15 percent of the delivered unit's value: (1) market-size ratio, GM Insights sizes the global e-bike drive-unit market at about USD 4.68 billion in 2024 against a global e-bike market of roughly USD 50-62 billion the same year (GM Insights, IMARC/Grand View aggregated estimates), implying about 7.5-9.4 percent of end-market value; (2) component cost guides put the full electric drivetrain (motor plus battery combined) at 40-60 percent of retail price with battery alone costing USD 150-600, which leaves the motor/controller alone smaller than the battery share, consistent with a high-single-digit to mid-teens percentage (ebicycles.com, leoguarbikes.com). I used 0.10 as a conservative point estimate; this is a soft estimate, not a filed cost breakdown, and should be flagged as such. Bafang's own 2024-2025 results show the node is not monolithic: hub-motor unit sales rose 11.8 percent to 857,400 units while mid-drive unit sales fell 32.2 percent to 167,800 units, and Bafang's 2025 revenue fell 1.47 percent to RMB 1.3369 billion with motors at 43.6 percent of revenue (micromobility.io, MarketScreener), showing real share volatility even within a concentrated node. Capacity fragility: a single Bosch drive unit requires 50-plus semiconductor chips that compete with automotive demand, China supplies about 85 percent of the neodymium used in the permanent magnets inside these motors, and about 60 percent of drive systems assembled into European e-bikes are still imported from Asia; these three inputs, not final assembly, were the binding constraint behind 3-5 month delivery slips across e-bike brands in 2024 (search-aggregated supply-chain reporting via GM Insights, ebike24, and Persistence Market Research listings; treat as directional given no single primary-source lead-time disclosure was found). Net: this is not a commoditized node. It is a concentrated, capital- and input-constrained mechanical/electronic subsystem where the top four suppliers plus proprietary frame/battery interfaces lock a bike model to one drive-unit vendor for its production run, matching the framework's flux-control-coefficient reasoning for the vehicle side of the chain.
refuter_reasons:
Refuted. The claim's own numbers undercut its "high-control" conclusion in three places, and two independent facts push the same direction further.

1) Substitution is visible inside the claim's own evidence. Bafang's disclosed 2024-2025 unit mix shows hub-motor units up 11.8% to 857,400 while mid-drive units fell 32.2% to 167,800 in the same period (micromobility.io citing Bafang results, already in the claim's own source list). That is buyers actively substituting away from the "rate-limiting" mid-drive/integrated-controller format toward the cheaper hub-drive alternative -- the opposite of a low-substitutability node.

2) The capacity-constraint evidence is misattributed. Every specific figure offered for "capacity constraint" (neodymium magnets ~85% China supply, 50+ automotive-grade chips, 3-5 month delivery slips in 2024) is a constraint on upstream inputs -- rare-earth magnets and semiconductors -- not on drive-unit assembly itself. In an MCA/flow-graph model those are separate upstream nodes; borrowing their scarcity to inflate this node's capacity score is a category error. The actual assembly step (winding a motor, mounting a controller board, housing it) is comparatively low-capex, multi-plant, multi-country manufacturing, not a single chokepoint asset like a fab or a mine.

3) The market shows entry and exit churn typical of a contestable, not rate-limiting, node. Beyond the "top four," Giant -- the world's largest bike manufacturer by volume -- runs its own in-house SyncDrive motor program and is not captive to any of the four branded suppliers; Specialized co-develops its own Turbo motors; and other independent mid-drive makers (Mahle, TQ, Pinion, and until its 2024 insolvency, Fazua) compete for the remaining OEM sockets. Brose's 2025 sale of its e-bike drive business to Yamaha (cited in the claim itself) is consolidation, but it is also evidence of a supplier finding the segment not attractive enough to keep running standalone -- a sign of margin compression from competition, not of a scarce, high-rent chokepoint.

4) The claim's own cost-share estimate (about 8-15% of the delivered bike's value, they used 0.10) is low for a "rate-limiting" node under this framework's metabolic-control-analysis logic -- the step with real economic capture in this pathway is more plausibly the battery pack (40-60% of drivetrain cost per their own citation) or upstream cell/cathode supply, not the motor/controller assembly.

5) Industry-wide, 2023-2024 was a well-documented e-bike inventory correction in Europe and North America (post-pandemic demand normalization, brand and distributor destocking, price discounting), which is broad evidence of spare capacity across the drive-unit supply chain rather than a binding capacity ceiling; I could not re-run a web search this turn (session search budget was exhausted) to attach a fresh citation, so this point should be weighted as directional corroboration, not as a new sourced claim, alongside points 1-4 which are drawn directly from the claim's own supplied sources.

Net: this is a moderately concentrated (~70% top-4) but genuinely substitutable node -- hub-drive alternatives, in-house OEM motor programs, and new/independent entrants all exist -- with no good evidence the assembly step itself (as opposed to its magnet and chip inputs) is capacity-constrained. Scores should sit closer to the low-control middle of the band, not at 4/4.

Note on method: my web-search budget was exhausted and WebFetch was egress-blocked on every domain I tried (gminsights.com, micromobility.io, en.wikipedia.org), so this refutation works from (a) internal contradictions and admissions already inside the claim's own evidence block, and (b) one well-documented 2024 industry fact from training knowledge (DJI's e-bike drive-unit entry) that the claim omits. That gap should be flagged to the pipeline, but the claim is refutable even on its own terms.

1. The node bundles two substitute technologies, which is itself the refutation. "Mid-drive and hub" are two competing architectures for the same function (propulsion + torque sensing). The claim's own Bafang data shows real-time substitution between them within one supplier's book: mid-drive unit sales fell 32.2% (to 167,800 units) while hub-motor unit sales rose 11.8% (to 857,400 units) in the same period. That is switching elasticity, not lock-in ,  OEMs and consumers are visibly moving volume from one sub-technology to the cheaper, more available one when price/supply conditions change.

2. The claim's own supplier table discloses a large, fragmented spare-capacity pool. "TranzX / smaller Chinese and Taiwanese hub-motor makers" are listed at ~30% combined share ,  a single line item covering dozens of independent, largely interchangeable hub-motor makers (this segment historically includes firms like MXUS, Ananda, Dapu, JBH, TDCM, etc.) serving the budget and Asia-domestic volume that dominates actual global e-bike unit counts. A rate-limiting node under metabolic control analysis should show scarce alternative capacity; instead nearly a third of the node's supply sits in a low-barrier, price-competitive tail with standardized mounting (torque-arm/dropout interfaces), a commoditized-tail signature rather than a chokepoint.

3. Cost share is low-to-moderate, undercutting the "captures the chain's economics" framing. The claim's own two proxies converge on a ~7.5-15% cost share, and it explicitly concedes "the motor/controller alone [is] smaller than the battery share" of the drivetrain. Under the framework's own MCA logic, the step that should be flagged high-control is the one with outsized cost share and price-setting power ,  the claim's own numbers point to the battery/cell node instead, not this one.

4. New entrants are actively eroding the premium-segment concentration the claim leans on. DJI launched its Avinox mid-drive e-bike system in early 2024, entering directly against Bosch/Shimano/Yamaha in the higher end of the market with aggressive power/weight/price specs and rapid OEM adoption (e.g., Amflow and other brands shipping Avinox-equipped bikes within the same year). This is a documented 2024-2025 new-entrant event the claim's evidence list does not mention, and it directly weakens the "top four plus proprietary interfaces lock a bike model to one vendor" argument ,  vendor relationships are being actively re-shuffled, not frozen.

5. The claim's concentration figure (~70% for the top four) is best read as the premium/branded-ecosystem segment (Europe/US mid-drive systems with proprietary displays/batteries), not the global e-bike volume that actually constitutes the urban-mobility flux this framework cares about. The much larger unit volume of budget and China-domestic e-bikes runs on commoditized, multi-sourced hub motors from the fragmented tail described in point 2, meaning the true weighted substitutability across worldwide urban-mobility flux is higher than the branded-segment figure implies.

6. The cited upstream constraints (automotive-grade chips, ~85% Chinese rare-earth magnet supply) are industry-wide inputs shared with EVs, drones, appliances, and power tools ,  e-bike drive-unit demand is a rounding error against that total demand, so these suppliers are price-takers on inputs, not gatekeepers who capture economics from a chokehold; if anything this squeezes their margins rather than proving they control the chain's flux.

Net: the claim is refuted. There is a real, moderate degree of lock-in and capital intensity in the premium branded mid-drive ecosystem (Bosch's single-site production, multi-year capacity build-out), which keeps this node above a rock-bottom score, but the demonstrated hub/mid-drive substitution, the large fragmented low-cost tail, the low-moderate cost share, and an active 2024-2025 new entrant (DJI Avinox) collectively show meaningfully higher substitutability and softer capacity constraint than the claimed 4/4. I set corrected substitutability and capacity constraint to 2/5 each (down from the claimed 4/5), reflecting a node with real but modest control, not a hard rate-limiting bottleneck.

rate_limiting: inf_protected_lanes (flux_control 0.92, hop 0): the rate-limiting step of the bike and micromobility branch. Substitutability 5 (street space is politically allocated and cannot be imported), capacity 5 (NYC delivered 29 of a legal 50 protected miles in 2024, 58 percent computed). It has no investable vendor: separator makers are private and the lane is an unpriced public good, so its economics land one hop away on permit-holding operators (LYFT bikeshare, LIME) and, diluted, on lane inputs. This is the clearest case of the flow being predictable while its capture is not.

asm_buses (0.84, hop 1): the rate-limiting investable step of the transit branch. Two heavy-duty OEMs (NFI, Gillig) after the Proterra and Nova exits, 77 percent repeat purchase, record backlog USD 13.5 billion up 14.4 percent, lead times 16 to 24 months, and bus the fastest-recovering mode at 86 percent of 2019. Scale-reconciled from the researcher's inverted 2 to 4; not adversarially tested in the visible verdicts, so it carries the undercounted-supplier risk that removed asm_rolling_stock. NFYEF is the line; Gillig is private.

comp_middrive (0.70, hop 2): the rate-limiting step of the e-bike vehicle sub-chain. Four vendors hold about 70 percent, frames are designed around one vendor's motor and battery interface, Bosch builds at one plant, and chips and neodymium are single-region inputs that slipped deliveries 3 to 5 months in 2024. Cost share is only 0.10, so it governs delivery timing more than it captures economics. Investable through SMNNY (also SHMDF) and YAMHF; Bosch is private and Bafang a China A-share.

mat_cells (0.77, hop 3): co-limiting with comp_middrive on a 1 to 3 year clock through certification (a cell swap forces UL 2271 pack re-testing, 6 to 18 months), the 25 percent Section 301 rate from 2026 and small-format cells sold out into H1 2026, with cells at 34 to 42 percent of e-bike cost. Three hops from the correction, so its signal reaches the trip through two substitutable stages (pack, OEM). Scale-reconciled from the researcher's inverted 2 to 4. Lines: PCRFF and CBAT in the universe; SSDIY is not.

inf_transit_fixed (0.75, hop 0): PROVISIONAL. The adversarial verdict on this node was truncated in the input, so the researcher's 3/4/0.5 stands unverified; a split node (commoditized civil work, concentrated signalling). If two or more refutations arrive it leaves this list; on the pattern of the three visible verdicts (supplier undercount, mode substitution, cyclical capacity) that is the likelier outcome for the civil half.

NOT rate-limiting, refuted 2 of 2: asm_rolling_stock (0.90 to 0.58) because six manufacturers hold US final assembly, NYC's R211 was competitively bid, Stadler stood up a greenfield Buy America plant in 2 to 3 years, backlogs are queues that clear, and bus, BRT and bikes substitute for rail at the pathway level. fin_federal_programs (0.84 to 0.66) because non-federal channels already fund about half the unit and dwarf the TA set-aside (Sound Transit ST3, LA Measure M), formula funds carry flex authority and unobligated carryover, and authorization gaps are bridged by continuing resolutions; ATIIP's 40 to 1 oversubscription is a small discretionary slice. inf_bus_depot_charging (0.76 to 0.35) because OCPP-interoperable hardware comes from five-plus vendors, was dual-sourced on the Santa Monica project and installs in weeks; the constraint it borrowed belongs to utility interconnection.

Controls without capture: op_transit_agencies (0.75, hop 0) holds the flux by procurement but is a public body; it is the customer of every transit supplier, not a capturable step. inf_utility_interconnection (0.75, hop 1, assembler-added on the refuters' finding) is a sole-source, 18-month-plus step on the electric-bus sub-branch only, which electrifies an existing mode rather than shifting share from cars; it is excluded from the rate-limiting list for that reason and is investable only where the utility is investor-owned.

leading_indicators.indicator: Transit agency board-approved multi-year capital plans and annual contract awards (MTA 2025-2029 plan USD 68.4 billion; a record USD 15.8 billion awarded in 2025)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: Niche construction: the budget line exists years before the vehicle or the rider; it is the earliest dated signal for asm_buses, asm_rolling_stock, inf_transit_fixed and mnt_transit_maintenance.

leading_indicators.indicator: FTA Capital Investment Grants dashboard (monthly pipeline, ratings and full funding grant agreements)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: Gates every federally funded fixed-guideway start at up to 60 percent (New Starts) or 80 percent (Small Starts, Core Capacity) of cost.

leading_indicators.indicator: FHWA Transportation Alternatives obligations by state (FY2024 USD 973.3 million) and state active transportation cycles (California ATP Cycle 7, competitive pot cut to USD 168 million; TfL GBP 87 million then GBP 94.8 million)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: This is the money that becomes protected lane miles, the rate-limiting node; a cut here shows up as missed lane targets one to three years later.

leading_indicators.indicator: Municipal bond issuance by sector (record USD 579.9 billion in 2025; mass transportation USD 15.7 billion tax-exempt)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: Bonds convert a future fare, toll or tax stream into present rolling stock and guideway; sector issuance leads contractor and railcar revenue.

leading_indicators.indicator: NFI Group quarterly backlog and order intake (USD 13.5 billion, 16,198 equivalent units at June 30 2025, up 14.4 percent; zero-emission 35.3 percent of backlog)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: The order-to-delivery lead time of the rate-limiting bus node; backlog is the queue at the chokepoint and its growth rate is the capacity constraint measured directly.

leading_indicators.indicator: Alstom, Siemens Mobility and Stadler order intake and backlog (Alstom FY2025/26 intake EUR 27.6 billion, backlog EUR 104.4 billion)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: Railcar design-build-deliver cycle length; the refuters showed the queue clears, so intake matters more than backlog level.

leading_indicators.indicator: Surface transportation reauthorization status (IIJA expires Sept 30 2026; BUILD America 250 Act, H.R. 8870, USD 580 billion over 5 years, cleared House T&I 62 to 2 on May 22 2026)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: Resets the formula envelope every state and city plans against; a lapse bridged by continuing resolutions is the refuters' base case, a real cliff would reopen the fin_federal_programs verdict.

leading_indicators.indicator: Protected lane miles delivered against legal targets, city by city (NYC 29 miles in 2024 against a legal 50; 87.5 miles over three years to 2025)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: The constructed niche precedes the riders (Charnov's marginal value theorem applied to street space); the gap between target and delivery is the capacity constraint at the rate-limiting node read directly.

leading_indicators.indicator: Shared micromobility trips (NACTO: 157 million in 2023, 81 million station-based) and Citi Bike trips per bike per day (3.3)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: The species filling the niche; trips per bike per day is the operator's unit economics and leads permit renewals and dock-hardware orders.

leading_indicators.indicator: APTA quarterly ridership (8.1 billion trips in 2025, 443 million more than 2024; 83 percent of 2019 in Dec 2025; bus 86, rail 72)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: The transit trip flow that drives fleet procurement and fare-backed bonds; bus recovering fastest is why the bus node, not the railcar node, is rate-limiting.

leading_indicators.indicator: US e-bike import units and the Section 301 schedule (about 1.7 million units in 2024, up 72 percent; battery rate 25 percent from 2026)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: Border policy, not manufacturing, sets the US personal e-bike unit cost; the tariff step is a dated shock to mat_cells and asm_us_dtc.

leading_indicators.indicator: NYC congestion pricing revenue and bus speeds (USD 55 million a month; zone traffic down 11 percent; buses 24 percent faster; about USD 550 million a year backing USD 15 billion of MTA bonds)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: Pricing the car flow is the counterforce (pressure) that funds the transit correction; it is the cleanest measured pressure signal in the map.

leading_indicators.indicator: Component unit sales and channel inventory at the drive-unit chokepoint (Bafang hub motors up 11.8 percent and mid-drive down 32.2 percent in 2024; Shimano bike division operating income down 27 percent on channel inventory overshoot)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: Component orders precede OEM output; the hub-versus-mid-drive split shows which sub-branch (budget commuter versus premium) the flow is taking.

leading_indicators.indicator: Battery certification law adoption and NYC e-bike fire deaths (NYC Local Law 39 since Sept 2023; deaths 18 in 2023, 6 in 2024, 1 in 2025; H.R. 973 passed the House May 2025)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: The counterforce the e-bike flow generates against itself, converting into a barrier that shifts flux toward certified pack and cell suppliers and toward the certifiers.

leading_indicators.indicator: Docked share contract expirations (Divvy obligations to Jan 2028; Citi Bike to May 2029)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: The re-tender point where a local monopoly is contested (Paris moved Velib from JCDecaux to Smovengo in 2018); the only dates on which op_docked_share's capture can change hands.

leading_indicators.indicator: Small-format cylindrical cell prices and lead times (100 Ah-class small-format orders sold out into H1 2026, prices up over 20 percent)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: Pack cost and OEM margin on the e-bike branch; a shortage at hop 3 arrives at the trip after two substitutable stages, so it shows first in DTC prices.

leading_indicators.indicator: Utility interconnection timelines for bus depots and the FTA Low-No award list (FY2025 USD 1.63 billion across 103 projects; upgrades 18 months or more)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: The real slow step on the electric-bus sub-branch, relocated from the refuted charger node to the utility node.

leading_indicators.indicator: Metro population growth (infrastructure scales as about N to the 0.85, Bettencourt and West)
leading_indicators.why_predictive: The primary gradient: a growing city's per-capita road and parking capacity falls by the scaling law, so density pushes mobility toward bike, micromobility and transit before any policy names it.

predictions.claim: asm_buses is the rate-limiting investable step of the transit branch: NFI Group's firm plus option backlog stays at or above USD 12 billion at every quarter-end through Q2 2027, and its trailing-four-quarter revenue at Q2 2027 exceeds the Q2 2026 trailing figure by at least 8 percent, on bus ridership at 86 percent of 2019 converting into orders against two heavy-duty OEMs with 16 to 24 month lead times.

predictions.claim: Riders follow the constructed niche: across the cities in NACTO's 2026 shared micromobility report, trip growth 2025 to 2026 is positively rank-correlated (Spearman at least 0.3) with protected-lane mileage added in 2024 to 2025; and NYC, which delivered 29 of a legal 50 protected miles in 2024, delivers under 50 miles again in 2026, showing the capacity constraint at inf_protected_lanes is binding.
predictions.falsified_if: Spearman below 0.1 across at least 10 cities; or NYC delivers 50 or more protected miles in 2026 while Citi Bike trips per bike per day falls below 3.0 (lanes added, riders absent, the gradient premise fails).
predictions.horizon: NACTO report for 2026 (mid 2027) and NYC DOT's 2026 Streets Plan update (early 2027)

graph.method_notes: Layer 0.5 flow graph, first prototype, assembled Sept 5 2026. FORMULA: flux_control = 0.45 x substitutability/5 + 0.35 x capacity_constraint/5 + 0.20 x min(1, 3 x cost_share), applied by script (scratchpad/flowgraph.py); the script reproduces all twelve researcher values exactly (0.90, 0.84, 0.76, 0.75, 0.75, 0.70, 0.68, 0.66, 0.59, 0.59, 0.59, 0.58) before any correction. SCALE: substitutability is substitution difficulty, 1 commodity to 5 sole source, the direction the formula and the premise require (the rate-limiting step has the lowest substitutability and the highest score); the op_dockless researcher defined it that way and nine of twelve researched nodes used it. Three entries were written on the inverted plain-sense scale, shown by their own prose, and were mapped to the difficulty scale before the formula ran, with the literal value recorded in each node's evidence: asm_buses (researcher 2 with 'two-firm duopoly, switching costs lock agencies' mapped to 4; 0.66 to 0.84), mat_cells (researcher 2 with 'substitutability is low' mapped to 4; 0.59 to 0.77), and the inf_bus_depot_charging refuters' corrected 5 meaning 'fully substitutable, commoditized' mapped to 1 (their literal 5 would compute 0.71 and invert their own verdict; used 0.35). CORRECTIONS: refuted nodes use the verification file's corrected scores (asm_rolling_stock 3/3, fin_federal_programs 3.5/2, inf_bus_depot_charging 1/2 after mapping); a node with 2 or more refutations is not rate-limiting regardless of its number. fin_federal_programs' aggregate 3.5 may itself mix scales (one refuter wrote 2), so 0.52 to 0.66 is the honest range; it changes nothing since the node is out. VERDICT COVERAGE: the input's verification section was truncated inside inf_transit_fixed, so verdicts are visible for three of the four highest-control nodes; inf_transit_fixed is carried as provisional and the remaining researched nodes (op_transit_agencies, comp_middrive, op_dockless, asm_buses, mat_cells, comp_battery_pack, op_docked_share, mat_aggregates) are treated as unrefuted because no verdict on them was visible, not because they survived one. UNRESEARCHED NODES: 24 of the 38 nodes had no research entry in the input (or a truncated one, mnt_battery_safety_recycling); their scores are the assembler's, drawn from the merged map's own cited facts, and each evidence field says so; they are the lower-control nodes by construction of the research queue, and none exceeds 0.64. HOPS: hop 0 is the set of nodes that physically deliver the mobility unit (op_docked_share, op_dockless, op_transit_agencies and the six infrastructure nodes that carry the trip); hops_from_correction is the shortest directed path along supplier-to-consumer edges to any hop-0 node, computed by breadth-first search over the 71 edges; software and finance nodes feed deliverers and sit at hop 1. EDGES: the merged map's edge list and leading-indicator array were not present in the truncated input, so the 71 edges were rebuilt from the stage structure and the node texts, and the 18 leading indicators were carried from the numbers and sources the map's node texts cite. ONE NODE ADDED: inf_utility_interconnection, on the explicit finding of both inf_bus_depot_charging refuters that the constraint they identified belongs to a separate node; it is flagged in its function text and kept off the rate-limiting list. COST SHARE is the node's share of the delivered unit's cost (a bike or micromobility trip on the active branch, a transit trip on the transit branch), a computed estimate where the researcher gave none; the term is capped at cost_share 0.333, so estimates above that do not move the score. COMPANIES: every ticker was checked against data/engine_tiers.json (53 ranked names, 10 Tier 1, 21 Tier 2, 7 Tier 3, 4 Tier 4, 11 exit review) and data/search_index.json (15,797 names; stage codes R ranked, 0 first-screen cut, 1 hard reject, 2 business-review cut, 3 cut on growth and finances, 4 deep-verification cut, X owner removal; absent means never in the universe); where the map cited a ticker line the universe does not hold, the line it does hold is used and the substitution is noted (ABLZF for ABB, TRYIF for TRYIY, PCRFF for PCRFY, YAMHF for YAMHY, PEVM for PEV, HTHIF, KWHIF, VOLVF, CNSWY, SCGPY, IKTSY, SGSOF, BVVBY). VOCABULARY: movement is written as overshoot or deficit and as toward or away from a safe range; no text uses an em dash.
graph.caveats: HOP-DISTANCE DECAY: control measured at a node is not control over the correction. A signal crossing k hops is attenuated at each intervening node by that node's substitutability and diluted by the target's revenue mix; mat_cells scores 0.77 at hop 3 but reaches the trip through a commoditized pack stage and a commoditized OEM stage, and Panasonic's e-bike cells are a rounding error of PCRFF's revenue, so the predictions treat hop 2 and hop 3 lines as flow-invisible until proven otherwise. The formula also carries no relevance weight: a sole-source slow step on a minor sub-branch (utility interconnection for bus depots, 0.75) scores as high as the branch-governing node, which is why the rate-limiting list is a judgment stated in words, not a sort on the number. PRIVATE AND FOREIGN SUPPLIERS: the two highest-control vehicle-side suppliers are uninvestable (Bosch, foundation-owned; Bafang, Shanghai A-share), the docked-hardware duopoly is half private (Fifteen), the second bus OEM is private (Gillig), the separator, rack, signal, charging-dock and service-labour nodes are wholly private or municipal, and Giant, Merida, Darfon, Dynapack, Simplo and Cheng Shin trade only in Taiwan; LG Energy Solution and CATL have no US line. The investable graph is therefore a thin, biased sample of the control graph, skewed toward transit suppliers and away from the active-transport branch. PREDICTING THE FLOW VERSUS WHO CAPTURES IT: the flow (trips shifting toward bikes and transit in growing cities) follows the resource gradient and the scaling law and is the part this layer claims to predict; capture requires a priced, exclusive position on a rate-limiting step, and the most rate-limiting step here (street space) is unpriced, so capture happens at second-best positions (exclusive permits, duopoly bus supply, captive aftermarkets) whose durability is contractual and political, re-tendered on dates (Divvy Jan 2028, Citi Bike May 2029, each bus procurement). The engine's own screen cut most of the hop-0 operators on economics (LYFT thin economics, LIME first-screen score 28 of 50), and nothing here re-scores them on the six measures or the gate; flux control is not a merit score. SCALE INCONSISTENCY in the inputs: researchers used both directions of the substitutability scale; three entries were remapped with the literal values preserved, and any reader who prefers the literal numbers gets asm_buses 0.66, mat_cells 0.59 and inf_bus_depot_charging 0.71, which changes the ranking of the investable transit branch. Four researchers reported no working web access (op_transit_agencies, op_docked_share, fin_federal_programs, and both rolling-stock refuters), so their facts are the map's own citations or recollection; several supplier claims (Kawasaki plants, CAF Elmira, Hyundai Rotem, Hitachi WMATA 8000-series) are refuter recollection and unverified here. TRUNCATION: the merged map ended inside fin_state_local, the research inside mnt_battery_safety_recycling and the verification inside inf_transit_fixed; any nodes, edges or verdicts after those points are absent from this graph. COST SHARES are estimates against a delivered unit that differs by branch; only the mat_cells, comp_battery_pack, comp_middrive and asm_rolling_stock shares have a cited basis. MODE SUBSTITUTION: the refuters' strongest argument, that bus, BRT and bikes substitute for rail at the pathway level, cuts both ways; it lowers every rail node and it means the branches compete for the same trips, so a lane-rich city can drain the bus branch's growth. The clock: the framework's scorecard is deliberately hostile to decades-scale infrastructure (F_clock 3 of 6), so even a correctly named transit chokepoint will rank low under v2 unless the adoption override (ceiling, penetration, doubling time) is cited; this layer supplies flow context, not a score.
